class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Solution: Slope Fields", [

            "Think of this as directional winds.",

                                color="#00FFFF", buff=0, tip_length=0.1) 
                          for pos in grid_points])

        # Assets
        compass = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg")
        flag = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/flag.svg")
        
        # Labels
        wind_field_label = Text("Wind Field", font_size=20, color="#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1: Generate a grid of dots in #FFFFFF ===
        self.play(Create(dots))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2: Transform dots into small directional arrows ===

        self.place_at_grid(compass, 'A2', scale_factor=0.3)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Solving: Finding the Curve", ["We connect arrows to find solutions.", "Initial conditions fix a specific curve.", "They act as anchors for solutions."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Create arrows (slope field simulation)
        arrows = VGroup()
        for i in range(1, 6):
            for j in range(1, 6):
                arr = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*0.3 + UP*0.2, color=GRAY, buff=0).scale(0.5)
                self.place_at_grid(arr, f"{chr(65+i)}{j}")
                arrows.add(arr)
        self.play(FadeIn(arrows))
        
        # Show initial condition using asset
        # Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/anchor.svg
        point = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/anchor.svg", color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(point, "D2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        label = Text("Initial Condition", font_size=16, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(label, "C4", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(point), Write(label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # Trace path
        path = VMobject(color="#00FF00", stroke_width=4)
        path.set_points_smoothly([self.grid["D2"], self.grid["C3"], self.grid["B4"], self.grid["A5"]])
        self.play(Create(path), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # Highlight final curve
        final_curve = path.copy().set_color(WHITE).set_stroke(width=6)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(path, final_curve))
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: The Hook: Dynamics in Motion
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'change'. Start with a visual of a rabbit population growing or a robotic arm moving. Explain that instead of just knowing where an object is (position), we often only know how its velocity changes (acceleration/rate).
sections.example: A robotic arm's velocity changes based on the friction it encounters; we need an ODE to predict its exact path.

sections.title: Core Definition: What is an ODE?
sections.content: Define an ODE as an equation relating a function to its derivatives. Use a split-screen graphic: Left side shows a simple algebraic equation (x+2=5) as a 'snapshot', right side shows an ODE (dy/dx = ky) as a 'flow'.
sections.example: A water tank leaking: The rate of change of volume (dV/dt) is proportional to the square root of the height (Torricelli's Law).

sections.title: Visualizing the Solution: Slope Fields
sections.content: Prerequisite check: Basic understanding of slopes. Explain that an ODE defines a 'slope field'. Visualize this as a grid of tiny arrows representing the direction of the solution at any point.
sections.example: Imagine a flock of birds: The ODE is the 'wind direction' at every point; the solution is the actual path a bird takes as it flows with that wind.

sections.title: Solving: Finding the Curve
sections.content: Demonstrate how to 'connect the arrows' from the slope field to draw a specific solution curve. Emphasize that initial conditions (e.g., where the object starts) act like 'anchors' to pick one specific curve from the family of solutions.
sections.example: A ball tossed in the air: The ODE is constant gravity, but the 'Initial Condition' (initial height and throw speed) determines if it hits the ground or goes over a wall.

sections.title: Summary & Application
sections.content: Wrap up by highlighting that ODEs are the 'language of the universe'. From chemical reactions to bridge vibrations, ODEs translate how systems behave over time into mathematical models.
sections.example: Brief animation showing a heart rate monitor (ODE) stabilizing after medication, summarizing the predictive power of the discipline.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The current scale (1.2) is too large for the grid cells, risking clipping and poor margin spacing.
